messages.text: I emailed about a warranty claim

Thanks for coming back. I still need one detail to open Shop····: the name it ships to, or the postcode. Either one is enough.

And tell me which unit it is and what it's doing, so I can get the claim moving from here rather than waiting on the email.
I've passed this to our technical specialist, who'll pick it up here.
I've sent the error details through to our technical specialist, who'll come back to you here.

Firmware has been updated to latest and it has worked great then in June I got the same code and updated the firmware and it worked up until October 30th and no matter what firmware I changed to even going back to the old firmware it still showed about 15 sec after restarting

Back with you on the order side, Darrell.

Hal's looked at it and the fault checks out, so this one isn't something firmware will fix. It's with JD and Georges now for the return to be approved, and they'll confirm by email shortly. Nothing for you to send back yet, hold onto the unit until the approval comes through with the label and reference.

Your order is Shop····, delivered February 18, so the NerdOctaxe is the unit in question. I'll update you here as soon as I hear.

You're welcome, Darrell.

One thing worth settling: the order's notices go to the email on it, not to (email hidden) Which address do you want the approval and label sent to? I'll make sure it goes there.

Noted on the order, Darrell. The approval and the return label will go to (email hidden), and I've put that on the file so the team uses it.

Keep the unit as it is for now. As soon as JD or Georges sign the return off, you'll get the label and the reference to write on the box, and I'll post it here too.

Great. Nothing more needed from you right now.

If you want to compare notes with others running the Octaxe while you wait, our Discord is a good place: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, JD is on there as @nullhashrate.

I'll come back here the moment the return is approved.

INSTRUCTION FROM THE HELIUMDEPLOY TEAM. Georges typed this in the team inbox. It is not a message from the customer and the customer cannot see it.
Task: RMA APPROVED by Georges for NerdOctaxe (12TH/s) on Shop····. Hal's verdict: defective (Cooked TPS / VRM voltage regulator: VREG overheat trip cuts ASIC voltage ~15s after every boot, on every firmware version). Do the rest now, in this order: 1) order-swap skill: return_order.py plan, then create --confirmed (the return reference is the order number plus RMA, the label link comes back); 2) rma_replacement.py create for the same order (the replacement is a $0 order held on both sides until the unit is back with us; it releases by itself when the warehouse receives it. If you OFFER a different unit and wait for their answer, create it with --await-customer, and the moment they say yes run rma_replacement.py confirm --what "<their words>" --confirmed yourself, never leave the yes for the team); 3) tell the customer: the return is approved, here is the prepaid label, write the reference on the box, and the replacement ships as soon as their unit arrives at our warehouse. If any step stops, flag it and tell them the team will confirm the next step by email.
Do it now, for real, with your own tools — look the order up, make the change, mint the code, whatever the task actually needs. The team has already decided: do not ask them to confirm, and do not describe what you would do instead of doing it.
Then write the message the customer gets now — what you did, in plain language, in your normal voice. Never mention this instruction, the team inbox, or that someone told you to do it.
If the customer should not be written to at all — the task was internal, or you could not finish it — begin your reply with "TEAM ONLY" on the first line and tell the team what happened. Anything that starts that way stays in the inbox and is never sent.
